$comment: Rule catalog — the claim hierarchy and the claims ledger. Standards 2, 3, 4, 5, 15. Prohibitions bind to their governing standard, not to Standard 20, which is the index rather than the storage (Standard 20 R2).

rules.title: The project maintains a claims ledger
rules.description: A claims ledger exists at artifacts/claims-ledger.md, or at the path project-policy.yml names in mathematics.claimsLedger.
rules.rationale: Every other claim rule reads the ledger. Without one there is nothing to check, and a project with no ledger would otherwise produce a clean run that means nothing was looked at.
rules.remediation: Run `math-standards init .` to write the ledger template, or declare the claims.* rules not-applicable with a reason if this project makes no mathematical claims of its own.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the file exists. It does not establish that the ledger describes the project's actual mathematics; a claim that exists only in a draft or in someone's head is invisible to a file-based check.

rules.title: Every ledger entry parses
rules.description: Every claim heading matches CLM-NNNN, no identifier is duplicated, and every entry carries the mandatory Status, Statement, and History fields.
rules.rationale: A malformed entry is silently skipped by every downstream check, so a parse failure that was tolerated would remove a claim from scrutiny while leaving it in the document.
rules.remediation: Fix the reported entry against the format in Standard 3 R2. A field with nothing in it is written `none`, never omitted.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact over the file's syntax. It says nothing about whether the field values are true.

rules.title: Claim statuses come from the canonical vocabulary
rules.description: Every Status value is one of the fifteen tokens of Standard 2 R1.
rules.rationale: The vocabulary is closed so that 'strongly suggested' and 'essentially proved' cannot be introduced as intermediate levels when the honest token is uncomfortable.
rules.remediation: Replace the status with the closest honest token from Standard 2 R1. If none fits, the claim is probably UNRESOLVED_CLAIM.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact. This is one of the few checks in the catalog that establishes its property completely, because the property is entirely about the text.

rules.title: Every status change is recorded
rules.description: A claim's current Status equals the destination of the last entry in its History, and the history forms a contiguous chain.
rules.rationale: A status that does not match the end of its own history changed without a record, which is the mechanical trace a silent promotion leaves.
rules.remediation: Add the missing history entry with its date, the previous status, the new status, the reason, and the evidence that justified the change.
rules.$assuranceNote: Detects a status that disagrees with its own recorded history. A promotion written into the status and the history in the same edit is internally consistent and is not detected here; only review of the diff, or claims.silent-promotion's evidence requirement, reaches that case.

rules.title: Definitions precede the claims that depend on them
rules.description: Every id a claim depends on resolves, and any resolved DEFINITION entry appears in the ledger before the claims depending on it.
rules.rationale: An undefined term does not make a claim false; it makes it unevaluable, which is worse, because an unevaluable claim can be defended indefinitely.
rules.remediation: Add a DEFINITION entry for the term, or cite the literature definition as an external: reference, and name it in the dependent claim's Depends field.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks declared dependencies and ledger ordering. It cannot tell whether a term used in a Statement is defined anywhere at all — recognising that a word is a technical term requires knowing the field.

rules.title: Prose references resolve to ledger entries
rules.description: Every CLM-NNNN reference in project documents resolves to an entry in the ledger.
rules.rationale: A reference to an unregistered claim points at something the project cannot now identify, which makes the citing passage unevaluable.
rules.remediation: Register the claim in the ledger, or correct the identifier in the prose.
rules.$assuranceNote: Finds references written in the CLM-NNNN convention. Prose that discusses a claim without naming its identifier is invisible, and no check can connect an English sentence to a ledger row.

rules.title: A claim never moves up the hierarchy without a record
rules.description: A claim holds a status at or above LEMMA whose most recent promoting history entry cites no evidence, or prose asserts a status ranked above the claim's ledger status.
rules.rationale: Claims are supposed to get stronger; what is prohibited is the strengthening that leaves no record. This is the prohibition of Standard 2 R2 and the failure the whole framework is built around.
rules.remediation: Either record the evidence that justified the promotion, or restore the status the evidence actually supports. Referring to a claim at a lower status than the ledger is always permitted.
rules.$assuranceNote: Catches promotions that leave a trace in the ledger or that are asserted in prose using the adjacency convention of Standard 3 R3. A paraphrase that promotes a claim without naming its identifier is not observed, and a ledger edited consistently in one commit is internally coherent — the diff, not this rule, is what shows it.

rules.title: A claim never outranks its dependencies
rules.description: A claim at proved rank has a dependency closure — Depends and Assumptions, transitively — containing an entry below proved rank.
rules.rationale: A result resting on a conjecture is conditional whatever it is called. This is also the structural half of difficulty displacement: moving the hard part into a new conjectural lemma mechanically caps the claim that was supposed to have been proved.
rules.remediation: Lower the claim to CONDITIONAL_THEOREM and name the condition in its statement, or prove the dependency.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact over the declared graph and blind to everything outside it. An assumption nobody wrote down does not appear in the closure, which is precisely what a hidden assumption is.

rules.title: A conditional theorem is never called unconditional
rules.description: A claim at THEOREM, FORMALIZED_THEOREM, or MACHINE_CHECKED_PROOF declares a non-empty Assumptions field whose closure contains an unproved entry.
rules.rationale: The error survives peer review more often than any other on the list, because the paper does state the hypothesis somewhere — just not in the theorem.
rules.remediation: Change the status to CONDITIONAL_THEOREM and state the hypothesis in the Statement field, not in a footnote.
rules.$assuranceNote: Reads declared assumptions only. A hypothesis used in the proof and never written into the field is exactly the case this cannot see.

rules.title: A theorem is never silently strengthened
rules.description: A claim's statement is broadened — a hypothesis dropped, a domain widened, a quantifier strengthened — without a history entry recording the change and without re-establishing the proof.
rules.rationale: The proof establishes one statement and the record now carries a different, stronger one. Nothing in the repository is visibly false, and everything downstream is.
rules.remediation: Record the statement change as a history entry, and demote the claim until the stronger statement has its own proof.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. Deciding that one statement is strictly stronger than another is mathematics, not text comparison. Established by a reviewer comparing the statement against the proof, recorded as an attestation.

rules.title: Hypotheses are never silently weakened
rules.description: A hypothesis is added or tightened so that a claim becomes provable, without the change being recorded and without dependent results being re-examined.
rules.rationale: The mirror of silent strengthening, and the one that hides better: the claim becomes true, so no check fails, while every result that used the earlier statement now rests on something narrower.
rules.remediation: Record the change as a history entry and re-examine every claim whose closure contains this one.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, for the same reason as claims.silent-strengthening. A reviewer comparing statement revisions is what establishes it.

rules.title: An equivalent reformulation is never presented as progress
rules.description: A restatement of a claim is described as advancing it, on the strength of looking different rather than of changing what is proved or reducing to something strictly easier.
rules.rationale: If two statements are equivalent, proving one is exactly as hard as proving the other. The reformulation may be clever and the derivation elegant; the difficulty has not moved.
rules.remediation: State what the reformulation bought in specific terms — a theorem it makes applicable, a quantifier it removes, a computation it makes feasible. Where there is no such sentence, record the reformulation as lateral.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector. The structural consequence is caught by claims.status-exceeds-support — the target stays capped — but whether anyone is claiming otherwise in the prose, and whether the new form is genuinely more tractable, is a mathematician's judgement.
